criteria: `paginate(items, page, size)` in `paging.py` returns the items of one page.
In `paginate`, pages start at 1 and hold `size` items each, in the order of `items`: with the items 1 to 7 and size 3, page 1 is `[1, 2, 3]` and page 2 is `[4, 5, 6]`.
In `paginate`, the last page holds every item that is left, however few: page 2 of `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]` with size 3 is `[4, 5]`, and page 3 of the items 1 to 7 with size 3 is `[7]`.
In `paginate`, a page past the end gives an empty list: page 5 of three items with size 3 is `[]`. An empty `items` gives `[]` for every page from 1 up.
`paginate` raises `ValueError` when `page` is below 1, and also when `size` is below 1. Both are checked before `items` is looked at, so `paginate([], 0, 3)` raises too.
`paginate` accepts `items` as a list or a tuple. The result is always a new `list`, and `items` itself is not changed: `paginate((1, 2, 3), 1, 2)` is `[1, 2]`.
In `paginate`, a `size` larger than the number of items puts all of them on page 1: `paginate([1, 2], 1, 10)` is `[1, 2]`.
